confidence.note: No dated 2020 pricing pages, no form-specific free-to-paid benchmark, and no TAM report; archived pricing pages would raise it

gross_margin.note: Software: Stripe ~3% plus hosting; free users are a fixed hosting cost. ~93% (estimate).

ltv_cac.note: Organic CAC ~$60 gives LTV:CAC ~7.5 (estimate), but paid search would sink it; only the organic loop works.

pricing_power.note: Google Forms free and a generous own free plan anchor low; Pro must undercut Typeform's ~$40 ASP.

build_effort.note: A doc-style block editor plus logic, embeds and payments: about 2 months to a usable beta for two devs.

skills_match.note: Two developers: the build is their core skill; marketing and support are learnable.

capital_needed.note: Hosting from $7-25 per dyno per month; near-zero capital, fits a bootstrapped budget.

time_to_mvp.note: 8-10 weeks to a launchable editor (estimate); slower than a no-code test.

sales_cycle.note: Self-serve card checkout: a maker upgrades the day they hit a Pro feature.

channel_readiness.note: Channel exists: Typeform's 'powered by' badge was its top traffic source; no Tally audience yet.

search_demand.note: Mass need: Jotform 5M users (2019-07), SurveyMonkey 720,921 paying users (FY2019).

trend.note: Rising: SurveyMonkey revenue +21% (FY2019), Typeform revenue ~2x mid-2017 to mid-2018.

willingness_to_pay.note: Typeform ~40k paying customers at ~$40/month while users complain of rising prices.

free_alternatives.note: Google Forms is free with unlimited responses for basic forms (R5: free_alternative hit).

competitor_density.note: 10+ competitors incl. Typeform, Jotform, SurveyMonkey/Wufoo; strong leaders (R5 cap 3).

differentiation.note: Doc-style editing is a real but copyable UX difference; unlimited free is a pricing choice, not a moat.

legal_regulatory.note: GDPR processor duties (Art. 28 DPA) and EU VAT MOSS: compliance work, not a licence.

platform_dependency.note: Owns its product and badge channel; depends only on swappable Stripe and hosting.

market_risk.note: Forms are a durable, recurring business need, not a fad.

skills.note: Strong build skills; no stated track record selling SaaS.

assets.note: No audience, list or network stated.

interest.note: Motivation not stated; assumed curious builders.

tam.reasoning: Visible leaders' revenue: SurveyMonkey $307M (FY2019) + Jotform ~$54M ARR (2019) + Typeform ~$19M run rate (2018) = ~$380M, a lower bound

sam.reasoning: Self-serve form builders for makers and SMBs (Typeform + Jotform ~$73M plus Paperform, Wufoo, Formstack etc.), excluding enterprise survey spend: ~$100M

som.reasoning: 0.1% of SAM $100M in year 1 for two founders = $100k ARR

competitor_price_range.reasoning: Google Forms free; Typeform average price ~$40/month (2018 founder interview); no dated pricing pages for others

price.reasoning: Assumed Pro price below Typeform's ~$40 average price

variable_cost_per_unit.reasoning: Stripe ~3.1% blended (1.4%+€0.25 EU, 2.9%+€0.25 non-EU) = $0.9 + ~$1 infra and support per paying user

churn_monthly_pct.reasoning: Between Baremetrics' 7.7% SMB user churn (2017) and ProfitWell's 3-4% for larger plans (2019); low-priced self-serve plan

conversion_rate_pct.reasoning: Visitor to sign-up 10% x free to paid 2% (Jotform implied <3%: $54M ARR / $360 per year / 5M users)

cac.reasoning: Organic: ~200 founder hours x $30/h per 100 paying customers (Product Hunt, communities, badge loop). Paid search would be ~$9.88 CPC / 0.2% = ~$4,900

ltv_cac.reasoning: 452 / 60 on the organic channel only; below 0.1 on paid search

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: Hosting 2 x $25 standard dynos + ~$50 database (Heroku pricing) + ~$50 tools; founders unpaid

break_even_customers_per_month.reasoning: 150 / 27 = 6 paying customers for costs; ~220 to pay two modest salaries (€6k/month)

time_to_first_revenue_weeks.reasoning: 8-10 weeks build + launch + first upgrades within ~4 weeks

launch_reason: The founders are in Belgium, but the product sells online worldwide in English from day one; Belgium only sets the legal and VAT base.

rules_applied.effect: free_alternative hit: free_alternatives held at 2; strong_competitor hit: competitor_density held at 2 (cap 3); no score change

type_checks.note: SMB self-serve SaaS churns 5-8% a month (Baremetrics 7.7%, 2017); at $29/month, lifetime is ~17 months, so retention must be built in
A new form takes minutes to rebuild, so incumbents hold users mainly through existing embeds and integrations, not lock-in (estimate, no dated source)

cheapest_test: Landing page with a 60-second doc-style demo video, posted to Indie Hackers, r/nocode and Makerpad: 300 waitlist sign-ups and 10 annual Pro pre-orders in 7 days
kill_criteria: fewer than 150 waitlist sign-ups by day 7 -> rework the pitch before building
fewer than 5 Pro pre-orders at $29/month by day 14 -> rethink the paid plan
free-to-paid conversion below 1% after 90 days of launch -> change the Pro gate

rescue.change: Put a 'Made with Tally' badge on every free form and launch on Product Hunt, Indie Hackers and Notion/no-code communities
rescue.why: Turns the free plan into the channel (channel_readiness, ltv_cac), as Typeform's badge did
rescue.requires: A shipped free plan and a launch post

rescue.change: Gate a few high-value features (remove branding, custom domain, file uploads, team) in Pro and keep the rest free
rescue.why: Lifts free-to-paid conversion and pricing_power without killing the free hook
rescue.requires: Usage data on which features free users hit
